user_prompt:
What is the effect of phenobarbital compared with levetiracetam, each used as first-line anti-seizure medication, on all-cause mortality before hospital discharge in neonates (up to 28 days of age, term or preterm) with clinically or electrographically diagnosed seizures?

Effect measure: pool as a risk ratio (RR), phenobarbital divided by levetiracetam. RR > 1 means more deaths with phenobarbital (favours levetiracetam).

Outcome: number of infants who died from any cause between randomisation and hospital discharge (events) out of the number randomised or analysed in each arm (total).
- Use deaths during the initial hospital stay or NICU stay. Do not use mortality at 3, 6 or 12 months, or deaths after discharge.
- If a paper reports a count of zero deaths in an arm, record it as zero events with the arm's size (do not drop the study). If a paper does not report deaths at all, leave the study out rather than assuming zero.
- Be careful with arm labels. Many papers list levetiracetam first in tables or figures; assign arms by drug name from the group definitions, not by column position, and keep phenobarbital (or phenobarbitone) as the treatment group in every study.
- Use the number randomised to each arm as the denominator when the paper gives it; otherwise the number analysed.
- Trials in which infants who did not respond were switched to the other drug (cross-over or add-on): use the original randomised group for each infant.
- Multi-arm trials: include only the phenobarbital and levetiracetam arms. Ignore arms with other drugs (e.g. midazolam, phenytoin, topiramate, lidocaine).

Do not pool seizure control, time to seizure cessation, EEG outcomes, adverse events, neurodevelopmental outcomes or mechanical ventilation. Include only randomised or quasi-randomised trials in neonates; exclude trials of seizure prophylaxis, trials in which neither arm is phenobarbital or levetiracetam, and comparisons of the two drugs as add-on therapy after failure of a first drug.
